QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_8

question.text: Short-selling Risk specific to Cat III AIFs includes:

answer.text: Losses from adverse price moves on short positions, stock-borrow costs, and added leverage/margin/mark-to-market risk

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes short selling and derivative short exposure as sources of risk for Cat III AIFs. Short positions can produce losses when prices move against the trade, require borrowing the underlying (with associated fees and costs), and add leverage through margining and mark-to-market settlement. These mechanics together define the short-selling risk profile a Cat III AIF must monitor. The Trap: "No risk" contradicts the basic mechanics of short selling. Reducing the answer to "only tax" or "only fund structure" misses the price, borrowing-cost, and leverage dimensions that the workbook actually highlights. Note: Short-sale mechanics, borrowing costs, and derivative margin/mark-to-market exposure are covered in the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
